title: SpARC: Token Similarity-Aware Sparse Attention Transformer Accelerator via Row-wise Clustering
problem: Self-attention mechanisms in transformers contain substantial row-level redundancies that cause computational waste. Attention scores exhibit high similarity within rows, enabling redundant computation that can be eliminated.
motivation: Self-attention accounts for a significant portion of transformer computation, making optimization critical for throughput and energy efficiency at scale.
method: SpARC exploits row-level redundancies through row-wise clustering where attention scores are calculated once per cluster rather than per token, achieving approximate attention. The approach is implemented as a fully pipelined accelerator architecture with a dedicated memory hierarchy optimized for high parallelism of the clustering-based computation.
key_novelty: Row-wise clustering approach that reduces self-attention computation by exploiting token similarity patterns within attention matrix rows.
contributions: Row-wise clustering method for approximate sparse attention achieving 85-90% sparsity with negligible accuracy loss
Fully pipelined accelerator architecture with dedicated memory hierarchy and high parallelism support
4× core attention speedup and 6× energy efficiency improvement over prior sparse attention accelerators
